title: Bench run-to-run variance and acceptance bands
description: The run-to-run spread of every published figure, and the acceptance band derived from it, produced by `python -m bench.variance` from committed manifests and run envelopes and nothing else. This exists because results.json pools every k=5 repetition into one cell figure, so the published numbers carry no recorded spread, and ADR 0030's fidelity gate ("figures within measured run-to-run variance of the committed ones") had no threshold behind it and could not be failed. This file is variance version 1.0.0 and validates 1.x documents only.
$comment: Two design points differ deliberately from results.schema.json. First, every entry carries its own `run_set`: results.json records one run_set on a file holding two concatenated run sets, which ROADMAP.md lists as v0.2.0 measurement debt, and there was no reason to repeat it here. Second, `entries[]` is keyed by (run_set, skill, skill_version, model, domain, metric) rather than one row per group, because a band is a property of a single metric and the four metrics of one cell have genuinely different widths. Consistency and clean_fp_rate are absent on purpose and not by oversight: score_consistency compares pairs of envelopes and is undefined for a single repetition, so no band for it can be produced by this method, and the published consistency floor therefore carries no uncertainty estimate at all.

run_sets.title: Run set identifiers, in the order given
run_sets.description: Every run set decomposed into this file. Each entry names its own, so a reader never has to infer which one a row came from.

method.title: How the band was estimated
method.description: Recorded in the file rather than only in prose, because a band read without its method is easy to over-trust.

estimator.description: Whole repetitions are resampled rather than individual artifact scores, because the published statistic is a ratio of sums across repetitions and artifacts, not a mean of per-repetition ratios; resampling whole repetitions preserves both that structure and the within-repetition correlation across artifacts.

draws.description: Bootstrap resamples. With k=5 there are at most 5**5 distinct resamples, so percentile resolution is coarse however high this is, and the band understates true uncertainty rather than overstating it.

seed.description: Fixed so the published band is reproducible byte for byte.

repetition_index_source.description: The repetition index is parsed from the envelope filename because no contract field records it. When that schema debt is paid, this string and bench/variance.py's parse_repetition_index change together.

covers.description: What the band measures, stated so a passing gate is not read as more than it is: repetition variance within one run set, not the transport, date, staging or isolation differences a re-run also carries.

verification.title: Whether the decomposition was checked against the published figures
verification.description: Pooling every repetition of a cell must reproduce the committed numerator and denominator exactly, or the decomposition is measuring something other than what was published. bench/variance.py refuses to emit a band when it does not, so a file with performed=false was produced without that check and its bands are unverified.

excluded_as_probe.title: Envelopes excluded as probe run sets
excluded_as_probe.description: Paths under a run set that share identity fields with the measurement grid but are not part of it, such as runs/steering/. Listed rather than silently dropped, because bench/results/README.md records this exclusion as a step in a recipe someone has to remember, and a file that does not say what it left out repeats that fragility.

entries.title: One entry per (run set, skill, skill version, model, domain, metric)

entry.title: The band on one metric of one cell

metric.description: Consistency is absent by construction; see this schema's $comment.

k.description: Repetitions this band was computed from. A band is only comparable to a re-run at the same k.

pooled.description: The published figure, recomputed here. Equal to the matching results.json value whenever verification.performed is true.

per_repetition.description: The figure each single repetition would have published on its own, pooled across the cell's artifacts. This is the evidence the band is derived from, kept so a reader can see the spread rather than take the interval on trust.

repetition_spread.description: repetition_max minus repetition_min: how far a single run swings, which is consistently wider than the band on the pooled statistic.

band_width.description: band_high minus band_low. A cell's discriminating power as a gate: a narrow band fails on a small shift, a wide one passes almost anything.
